10046749:
Barbara Howland Swan's Island LD 1731
I am Barbara Howland and I reside at 232 Minturn Road, Swan's Island, ME 04685.
I support requiring the Maine State Ferry Service to consult with Maine State Ferry Advisory Board on matters regarding budgets, strategic planning and operational decisions involving ferry services to the islands.
There is a compelling need for all who live on the Maine islands to have a strong voice in all matters involving the ferry service. Residents of island communities are deeply interested in all aspects of ferry service to the islands as we rely on ferry services for work, school, household fuel/propane deliveries, doctor appointments and most importantly ambulance runs. The ferry service provides our bridge, for young and old, to the mainland. It is inconceivable that persons with little or no knowledge of island living would be charged with oversight of the ferry service without significant input from island residents who are served by the ferries. Please act now to give a greater voice in the decision making of the Department of Transportation to the Advisory Boards that consist of island residents who are directly impacted by decisions regarding ferry service.

Testimony of Representative Holly Eaton in support of LD 1731: An Act to Increase the Influence of the
Maine State Ferry Advisory Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation Committee,
For the record, my name is Holly Eaton, and I represent House District 15, which includes Deer Isle, Stonington, Isle au Haut, Frenchboro, Swan's Island, Vinalhaven, Brooklin, Tremont, and Southwest Harbor.
I rise today in support of LD 1731, which strengthens the voice of island communities by requiring the Maine State Ferry Service to consult with the Ferry Advisory Board on key funding and operational decisions.
Before submitting our ferry-related bills this session, many of us representing islands in the 132nd Legislature met to discuss shared concerns about the Maine State Ferry Service. Together, we developed a coordinated set of proposals, designed not to compete with one another, but to give the Transportation Committee the opportunity to fully hear and consider the breadth of our island constituents' experiences.
While some of the bills may sound similar, that was intentional. Our goal was to present different pathways for the committee to explore, all aiming toward the same destination: a more accountable, reliable, and responsive ferry service for Maine's islands.
LD 1731 takes an important step toward this goal by ensuring that the Ferry Advisory Board -- made up of representatives from the very communities most impacted by ferry operations -- has a stronger, more formalized role in shaping decisions.
District 15: Brooklin, Deer Isle, Eagle Island Township, Frenchboro, Southwest Harbor, Stonington, Swan's Island, Tremont, Isle au Haut, Vinalhaven

For communities like Swans Island, Frenchboro, and Vinalhaven, ferry service is not an optional convenience. It is the connection to schools, medical care, jobs, groceries, and family. Decisions about routes, fares, schedules, and vessel needs must be made with our islands, not about them. I urge the committee to support LD 1731 and to continue listening closely to the voices of islanders who depend on the ferry system every single day. Thank you for your consideration, and I am happy to answer any questions.
District 15: Brooklin, Deer Isle, Eagle Island Township, Frenchboro, Southwest Harbor, Stonington, Swan's Island, Tremont, Isle au Haut, Vinalhaven

Holly Eaton House District 15 LD 1731

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation Committee, my name is Jeff Romano, providing testimony today on behalf of Maine Coast Heritage Trust (MCHT) in support of LD's 1231 and 1731.
It is not often that MCHT testifies before this committee. Our organization focuses on land conservation efforts, especially along the Maine coast and does not typically weigh in on transportation policy. However, for decades MCHT has worked with many of the island towns served by the State Ferry Service, including Frenchboro, Swans Island, North Haven, and Vinalhaven.
Through our conservation work in Maine's island communities, it has become clear that the long-term health and stability of each is dependent on a state-run ferry service that is responsive to their needs. There are many proposals before the committee this year that would be positive steps in that direction, including LDs 1231 and 1731.
MCHT encourages the committee to support both bills and to work closely with Maine's island communities to find a path forward that successfully balances their needs and that of the state.
Maine Coast Heritage Trust seeks to advance the conservation of lands and waters in Maine to ensure ecological wellbeing and foster thriving communities. Over the past five decades, we have conserved more than 185,000 acres, including over 160 places open for traditional outdoor recreation.

10047137:
LD1731 An Act to Increase the Influence of the Maine State Ferry Advisory Board on the Funding and Operations of the Maine State Ferry Service
Testimony in Support
April 29, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and members of the Transportation Committee, my name is Kimberly Grindle and I am a resident of Islesboro. I am submitting this letter today to express my support for LD 1731: An Act to Increase the Influence of the Maine State Ferry Advisory Board on the Funding and Operations of the Maine State Ferry Service
As a life-long resident of Islesboro and a small island business owner, I see firsthand how vital the Maine State Ferry Service is to island communities. Ferries for year-round residents are not a luxury they are a lifeline. They ensure access to essential services like healthcare, education, employment, and supplies. They also sustain tourism and local economies. However, the decisions about how this system is funded, scheduled, and operated often feel disconnected from the realities of island life and sometimes leave islanders feeling as though our voices are not heard during the decision-making processes.
LD 1731 is a commonsense bill that takes an important step toward aligning the Maine State Ferry Service with the communities it serves. By increasing the advisory board's role in decision-making--particularly in funding and operational planning--the bill recognizes the deep local knowledge and lived experience of island residents.
Too often, decisions are made without adequate input from those most impacted. Or are made with disregard to the input provided from island communities. This leads to impractical schedules, unexpected fee hikes, and service interruptions that destabilize island life. LD 1731 will ensure that island voices are heard--early, consistently, and meaningfully--when it comes to policies that shape their future.
Islanders are asking to be true partners in making this system work. LD 1731 honors that spirit and makes our ferry system more responsive, equitable, and sustainable for everyone.
I respectfully urge the committee to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 1731.
Thank you for your time and for supporting Maine's island communities.
Sincerely,
Kimberly Grindle

10047239:
Testimony of Island Institute in Support of LD 1731 April 29, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Transportation Committee, my name is Nick Battista, and I am testifying on behalf of Island Institute in support of the intent behind LD 1731.
Island Institute is a 42-year-old nonprofit organization based in Rockland, Maine. We boldly navigate climate and economic change with island and coastal communities to expand opportunities and deliver solutions. Much of our work takes place in the communities that are highly dependent on fishing, and the bulk of these communities are east of Damariscotta. The economy of these communities is closely tied to fishing and aquaculture, and these industries rely heavily on working waterfront infrastructure.
The Maine State Ferry Service serves 6 of Maine's 15 island year-round island communities. Recognizing the importance of the Maine State Ferry Service to Maine's island communities, between 2021 and 2023, Island Institute engaged KPFF, a nationally recognized transportation consulting firm with deep experience on ferry related issues to develop a series of reports and materials on the Maine State Ferry Service. This included the first demand driven study of the ferry service, as well as a deep dive into various operational issues. We worked closely with both Maine DOT/Maine State Ferry Service and a group of island community advisors who are very knowledgeable about how ferry related matters impact their community and who have spent years working to improve ferry service for their communities.
Here is a summary of existing transportation needs - https://www.islandinstitute.org/wpcontent/uploads/2023/04/Summary-of-Transportation-Needs-by-Island.pdf Additionally, through this process, KPFF also provided a set of Ferry Operator Best Practices - https://www.islandinstitute.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Ferry-Operator-Best-PracticesReview_DRAFT.pdf that includes a look at how other ferry services around the country handle 3 issues, funding and governance models, emergency transport options, and encouraging modal shifts from passenger cars to walk-ons.
Strengthening the role of the existing Maine State Ferry Service advisory board may help address some of the issues that arise between the Maine State Ferry Service and the needs of island communities. This isn't to say the advisory board isn't working well - the advisory board and the MSFS have, in recent years, had a more productive and collaborative working relationship. At the same time, these are complex issues and it is tough to meet the operational needs of the ferry service and also the needs of island communities. A stronger advisory board may be a way to help communities and the MSFS sort through these tough issues.

Before the Committee on Transportation

April 29, 2025

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and distinguished members of the Transportation Committee
My name is Nicole Grohoski, and I am honored to represent the 22 communities of Senate District 7
among them the islands of Swan's Island and Frenchboro -- two of the six islands served by the
Maine State Ferry Service. Thank you for the opportunity to present LD 173 l , "An Act to Increase
the Influence of the Maine State Ferry Advisory Board on the Funding and Operations of the Maine State Ferry Service," which aims to strengthen community engagement and improve the govemance
of this essential service.
For island residents, the ferry is not a luxury or convenience----it's a daily necessity. The ferry is their road to the mainland, their access to health care, education, commerce, and basic services.
When that connection becomes unreliable, it affects every facet of island life. In recent years,
service interruptions caused by staffing shortages have created hardship and uncertainty, making it clear that more must be done to ensure long-term stability and accountability.
LD 1731 proposes a simple yet meaningful shift: to give the Maine State Ferry Advisory Board a
more substantive role in decisions that directly affect the people it was created to represent. This bill would require the Ferry Service to engage the board in conversations about budgeting, planning, and significant operational changes. Topics like fare structures, scheduling, vessel maintenance, and overall rider experience would no longer be addressed in isolation--they would benefit from islander insight and feedback.
The legislation also introduces regular, structured reporting from the Ferry Service to the Advisory Board, including data on finances, service challenges, and rider satisfaction. The board
would be tasked with reviewing this information and submitting its own set of recommendations
to the Department of Transportation and to this Committee each January. These recommendations wouldn't be binding, but they would be part of the official record and must be meaningfully considered in future decision-making.

3 State House Station, Augusta, Maine 04333
State House (207) 287-1515 * Fax (207) 287-1585 * Toll Free 1-800-423-6900 * TFY 711
Nicole.Grohoski@legislature.maine.gov * legislature.maine.gov/senate

Impoitantly, LD 1731 does not propose expanding bureaucracy or spending more money. It
simply ensures that the voices of islanders -- and those who work most closely with them -- are
heard earlier and more often in the decision-making process. It adds transparency, structure, and accountability to a system that has too often left island communities feeling sidelined. Perhaps, if
this bill were already law, the DOT might have come to a different conclusion about
overnighting the ferries on the mainland. This is not about micromanagement; it's about shared stewardship. The state and the islands are partners in this public service, and it's time the relationship reflects that.
Thank you for your time and consideration of LD 1731. I'd be happy to answer any questions the
Committee may have.
